title: Office Plant Care Guidelines (Desk Jungle) — 2027
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

This page documents lightweight, community-driven guidelines for caring for office plants and maintaining a pleasant desk-plant ecosystem. It is intended to keep shared spaces tidy, reduce plant mortality, prevent pests, and provide clear escalation paths for issues.

These guidelines are informal, but some portions (noted below) are mandatory due to building rules, safety guidance, and vendor contracts.

Scope
- Applies to all plants in shared spaces (kitchen, conference rooms, lounges, phone booths, reception) and to potted plants kept at individual desks when they interact with shared facilities (water stations, plant shelves).
- Excludes customer office gardens and third-party contracted plant maintenance outside our leased floors.

Principles
1. Low-effort, resilient plants preferred: choose hardier species for communal areas (e.g., pothos, snake plant, ZZ plant).
2. Shared responsibility: Workplace Experience (Facilities) owns ordering and pest escalation; community volunteers support light weekly checks.
3. Non-judgmental culture: if a plant is wilting, flag it; no shaming.
4. Safety and building compliance: no aerosol pesticides or unauthorized chemical treatments in the office (mandatory).

Roles & Responsibilities
- Workplace Experience / Facilities (Workplace Lead): owns budget, vendor coordination, pest escalation, plant rotations, and supplies reorders.
- Desk Jungle Stewards (rotating volunteers): 1–2 people per floor who perform light weekly checks in shared-planter zones and update the Plant Log.
- Individual Employees: responsible for personal desk plants (follow Desk Jungle Guidelines below).

Weekly Care Schedule (recommended)
1. Monday: Steward inspects shared planters, notes soil moisture, removes dead leaves, and checks for fungus gnats/mites.
2. Wednesday: Spot-watering only if needed (no routine misting; see policy note below).
3. Friday: Tidy loose soil, confirm pots have trays, and record any issues in the Plant Log.

Policy note (2026 building update): Routine misting is no longer recommended in shared areas because it can trigger humidity-sensitive HVAC sensors and increase slip risk near hard floors. If a specific plant requires humidity support, Facilities will place it in an appropriate location or use vendor-approved methods.

Desk Jungle Guidelines (personal plants)
- Pot size: keep desk plants to 4–6 inch pots. Plants larger than 6 inches should be moved to a designated plant shelf or floor planter area (coordinate with a Steward).
- Drainage & trays (mandatory): pots must have drainage and must sit on a waterproof tray/saucer. No exceptions near laptops/monitors.
- Watering:
  - Prefer using the kitchen sink or designated watering station.
  - Do not water directly over carpeted areas.
  - If watering at your desk, carry the plant to/from the sink and let it drain before returning.
- Soil/repotting (mandatory): no repotting or loose-soil handling at desks. Repotting must be done at the designated potting area (if available) or offsite.
- Lighting: if a plant requires bright light, place near windows; avoid blocking walkways and emergency egress.
- Allergies/scent: avoid strongly fragrant flowering plants in open-plan seating. If a neighbor reports an allergy concern, relocate the plant without debate.
- Pets: if you work near office dogs, avoid placing known pet-toxic plants at floor level (e.g., some lilies). When in doubt, place the plant on a stable shelf.

Shared Planters & Conference Rooms
- Labeling: all shared planter pots should have either (a) a small waterproof label with plant name and last-watering date, or (b) a Facilities-provided QR label that links to the Plant Log entry.
- Rotation cadence: Facilities will rotate plants approximately every 8–12 weeks to refresh displays and reduce heat/sun stress. (Previously quarterly; updated based on vendor guidance.)
- Conference room rule (mandatory): no watering in conference rooms. If a plant needs water, move it to the watering station.

Supplies & Ordering
- Facilities maintains a basic kit: peat-free potting mix (for Facilities/vendor use), pruning shears, low-dose fertilizer, sticky gnat traps, trays/saucers, labels/QR tags, and disposable gloves.
- To request supplies or help:
  - Submit a request via Workplace Requests (Jira Service Management): see /confluence/facilities/workplace-requests
  - Non-urgent: add a note in the Plant Log so Stewards can batch requests.
- Emergency replacement (pests, flooding/leaks): contact Workplace Experience via the Workplace Requests “Urgent” category.

Pests & Health Issues
- Immediate action:
  1) Isolate the affected plant away from other plants (at least 10 feet when possible).
  2) Take photos (tops of leaves, undersides, soil surface).
  3) Update the Plant Log with time/date, location, and your name.
- Quarantine window (updated): keep suspected plants isolated for 14 days (previously 7–10). Most recurring office outbreaks we see require a longer observation period.
- Treatment (mandatory): do not use aerosol sprays, essential oil mixes, or “home remedies” in the office. Facilities will coordinate vendor-approved treatments and ensure compliance with building rules (see approved chemicals page).
- Escalation: if pests persist beyond 7 days or spread to multiple planters, Facilities will engage the plant vendor or building management.
- Disposal: do not compost onsite. Facilities will dispose of contaminated soil/plant material per building guidance.

Event Use & Decorations
- Temporary decorations (e.g., pot toppers, small plaques) are allowed but must be removed within 24 hours after the event (updated from 48 hours to keep shared spaces tidy).
- No open flames, glitter/confetti, or food-based decorations in shared planters.

Conflict Resolution
- If a plant in a shared zone is being mistreated or over-cared for (e.g., overwatering), leave a polite note in the Plant Log describing the issue and what you observed.
- If unresolved after one week, escalate to Workplace Experience, who will mediate and (if needed) relocate the plant.

FAQ
- Q: Can I rehome my unhealthy desk plant into a shared planter?
  A: No. Rehoming must be approved by a Steward after a quick assessment to avoid introducing pests/disease.
- Q: Who pays for a replacement plant I broke?
  A: Personal desk plants are the owner’s responsibility. Accidental damage to shared planters should be reported; replacement may be covered by Facilities depending on circumstances.
- Q: Can I bring in cut flowers?
  A: Yes, in personal areas. Please dispose of wilted flowers promptly and avoid strong scents in open-plan seating.

Appendix: Quick reference table

Plant Type | Best Location | Water Frequency | Notes
Pothos | Low light zones, shelves | Every 10–14 days | Very tolerant of neglect
Snake Plant | Very low light desks/shelves | Every 3–6 weeks | Avoid overwatering
ZZ Plant | Low to medium light | Every 2–4 weeks | Drought tolerant
Rubber Plant | Bright indirect light | Every 7–10 days | Trim to control size
Spider Plant | Medium light shelves | Every 7–14 days | Easy; can drop plantlets
